On Tue, Mar 20, 2028 at 8:22 AM david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — thank you for the heads up, and sorry for the customer impact. We're triaging now.

Quick technical snapshot (first-pass):
- Observed: KV cache pressure on node pool redwood-prod-gp2-01; sustained lock contention and slow mutex on the shared cache shard for the long-context sessions.
- Error signature: 502/504s emitted from proxy when token queue > ~1200 per-second sustained for > 90s.
- Likely trigger: recent traffic shift at Veridian (longer cart prompts, more system messages) causing larger KV footprint per request and pushing beyond configured continuous-batch window.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (order matters):
1) Route Veridian traffic to fallback pool with larger GPU memory (dedicated pool id: ded-ver-01). This reduces contention quickly.
2) Temporarily pin model variant to redwood-2-medium (reduces KV size) and disable prefix caching for long-checkout flows.
3) Increase proxy token-timeout to 6s while we monitor — gives transient headroom.

I've attached a short excerpt of the support log (support_log_20280320.txt) and a quick command list for ops. If we can get permission to route, I will trigger the change and report back within 10 minutes.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Veridian escalation - resolution summary and next steps

Team & Veridian — final update and customer-facing summary.

What happened:
- Between 07:30–08:10 PT on 2028-03-20 we observed sustained token queue backpressure for Veridian's workloads resulting in increased proxy timeouts and 5xx errors on checkout flows. Root cause: larger-than-expected KV footprint due to recent prompt changes coupled with cache shard contention on redwood-prod-gp2-01.

What we did (timeline highlights):
- 08:40 PT: Traffic routed to ded-ver-01 (higher-memory pool) and model variant pinned to redwood-2-medium.
- 08:50 PT: Proxy token-timeout increased to 6s for Veridian route while we monitored error rates.
- 09:10 PT: Errors returned to baseline (<0.5% of flows). We kept the fallback route for 24 hours to ensure stability.

Customer impact & remediation:
- Veridian reported ~18% checkout failures at peak; we issued a 10% service credit (applied to next invoice) and offered a follow-up architecture review.

Preventative actions:
- SREs to increase cache-shard monitoring and add autoscaling triggers for KV pressure (INF-4521).
- Product to provide a recommended prompt-size guide for high-throughput checkout flows for customers (owner: Laura).
- Ops to add a per-tenant circuit-breaker when token queue > 1000 for >60s (owner: Karthik).

Attachments: postmortem_summary_veridian_20280321.pdf (customer-friendly summary)
Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4521

Thanks to the team for a rapid response and to Veridian for the cooperative troubleshooting. If you'd like a synchronous readout, Laura and I can join your Tuesday leadership call.

—David Kim
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
